title: Snapshot Sprawl by VM
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`), uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=proxmox:metric event=snapshot
| stats count as snapshots, sum(snapshot_size_gb) as snapshot_gb by vm_name
| where snapshots>5 OR snapshot_gb>50
| sort - snapshot_gb
description: Lists virtual machines hoarding too many snapshots or too much snapshot storage, the classic tax of 'temporary' rollback points that never got cleaned up.
value: Snapshot clutter quietly consumes space and slows storage; a sprawl report helps you keep rollback safety without the long-term baggage.
implementation: Forward snapshot inventory data from Proxmox; review monthly and remove stale checkpoints that no longer serve a clear purpose.
visualization: Table of VMs by snapshot count and total snapshot size.
grandmaExplanation: It compares which virtual machines have piled up too many old safety snapshots and are wasting storage space.
